items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: I played with T-Bone back in the days when...at the Plantation... T-Bone and I used to ride down there... by the time you came to Europe in '68 with T-Bone

ctx.x: Now, how was that? You hadn't accompanied Blues singers much before.

Well, I played with T-Bone back in the days when...at the Plantation, when John Kirby was there. And also there was a fellow there working in a real estate office. His name was Norman Granz. And he got us to play concerts down at the high school in San Diego. And T-Bone and I used to ride down there, with Oscar Pettiford, Sir Charles Thompson, Red Nichols and his Pennies and Nat Cole...
You mean this is before Jazz at the Philharmonic.

items.title: 68239_Ram Ramirez oral history interview
items.q: That's after I went with Milt Buckner and T-Bone Walker... So T-Bone Walker and I knew each other from back in Los Angeles... Now, coming a little closer, you went to Europe in '68 with T-Bone Walker.

ctx.x: I think what we'll finish up with is your last five years, to see what you've been doing recently.
I've been going abroad with the Harlem Blues and Jazz Band. I went over twice to Europe. That's after I went with Milt Buckner and T-Bone Walker.
